text: Agents Notch 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 的 Windows 桌面状态面板，在屏幕顶部以置顶刘海显示会话工作中、等待关注、完成或失败等状态。host 监听全局会话事件，维护状态并发布给独立窗口。用户可以查看会话活动和上下文用量、打开指定会话，并配置显示器、位置、动效和显示行数。面板还会标示宿主心跳状态，帮助识别状态是否仍在更新。

Agents Notch is a Windows panel for DeepSeek Harness. Its always-on-top notch shows sessions that are working, waiting, done, or failed. A host publishes session events to a separate window. Users can inspect activity and context, open a session, and configure placement, display, and motion.
我想一眼看到哪些 DSH 会话正在等我处理。
有没有能把多个 agent 会话状态放在桌面顶部显示的面板？
我想在 Windows 桌面监控 DSH 会话是否运行、完成或报错。
能不能从桌面提示直接切换到需要处理的会话？
我想查看 agent 当前调用的工具和会话上下文用量。
有没有支持调整位置和显示器的 DSH 桌面状态挂件？
我想知道哪些 agent 遇到错误或已经完成。
有什么方式能让多个会话的状态在桌面始终可见？
按会话事件把工作中、等待关注、完成和错误分类为可展示状态；空闲会话不会仅因仍连接就占据面板行。这样用户能集中看到仍需处理或刚结束的会话。
host 将会话状态发布给独立 Windows 窗口，面板可展示活动信息和上下文，并提供打开对应会话的交互，便于从桌面返回 Harness 处理。
设置支持调整面板位置、目标显示器、行数、透明度、动效和已完成会话显示。设置值会经过范围约束，文件设置与插件配置共同决定窗口呈现。
host 管理独立窗口的启动和退出后重试；找不到窗口程序时仍持续提供状态，并记录可用于修复安装的提示，避免状态插件整体静默缺失。
host 可获取与插件版本对应的 Windows 窗口发布文件；发布提供 SHA256 文件时会校验下载结果，下载失败则保留状态服务并报告问题。
仅支持 Windows 10/11 x64，且需要兼容的 DeepSeek Harness。窗口是单独的桌面程序；可选的 session-finished 插件用于读取会话关闭状态，没有它时会采用超时回退。

dsh-agents-notch README · Introduction：

**An always-on-top notch for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) that answers one question: which of my sessions needs me right now?** [](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-agents-notch) [](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) [](#requirements) [](LICENSE) [Install](#install) · [What it shows](#what-it-shows) · [Configure](#configure) · [Limits](#limits-stated-plainly) · [Develop](#develop) · [中文](#中文)
dsh-agents-notch README · Introduction：Recorded from the window itself (--record), frame by frame — not a mock-up.

dsh-agents-notch README · Why：If you run more than a couple of sessions, finding out whether anything is waiting on you costs a
context switch every time:

| what you do today | what it costs |
|---|---|
| alt-tab between windows and read each sidebar | the thing you were doing, every time |
| wait for a desktop notification | one per session, and none of them say which one is *blocked* |
| leave the sidebar visible | it is only visible when the app is in front — which is when you do not need it |

dsh-agents-notch README · Why：The notch is a small always-on-top tab that **never takes focus**, **hides under a full-screen app**, and
shows the one thing the sidebar cannot while you are in another window: **a session stuck on you**. When
one gets stuck, the tab grows into an alert that says why, with an **Open** button that switches the app
to that session — from wherever it is, minimized or in the tray. And it **never gets in the way**:
pass over it and it fades and lets your click through; rest on it and the board unfolds.

dsh-agents-notch README · What it shows：
That strip is the whole visual language. **Working** wears a slow blue arc and nothing else, because working is the quiet default — and while any session is running a tool, light runs along the tab's lower edge. **Needs you** wears amber, **done** green, **failed** red. Every session keeps its own colour on the bot's rim, so three sessions read as three sessions rather than three copies of one.

dsh-agents-notch README · It never gets in the way：
The tab sits where you reach for tabs and title bars, so it steps aside. A pointer **passing over** it turns it into a faint ghost that clicks go straight through — to the browser tab or the menu under it. Only a pointer that **rests** there for 1.6 s unfolds the board, and pushing it against the top edge of the screen opens it at once. All three are settings (`hoverMode`, `holdMs`, `topEdgeOpens`); `open` brings back unfold-on-hover.
section: It never gets in the way

text:
dsh-agents-notch README · The tab speaks up：
When something **new** happens — a session asks for you, fails, or finishes — the tab grows into an alert for a few seconds and then folds back. **Open** takes you straight to that session. Only fresh events are announced: a question that has been waiting for an hour is on the board, not in your face.

dsh-agents-notch README · The board：Rest the pointer on the tab, or push it against the top of the screen, and the board unfolds. At the top is the session that **changed most recently**, so a
finish or a question is what you see first: its title, its project and age, how full its context is, and
one line of what it is doing — the tool it is running and the step, the question it is asking in full,
or how it ended. Below it, every other session in one list: what it is doing in a word and how long ago.
More sessions than fit? The list scrolls.

dsh-agents-notch README · The board：**Click** a row to put that session on the big bot. **Double-click** a row, or press **Open ↗**, and the
app switches to it. A finished or failed row has a **✕** that closes it out — the same as ticking it in
the app.

dsh-agents-notch README · Sixteen faces：The bot's face is the state, read closer. A working bot is **focused** in a tool and **thinking** between
tools, **determined** on a long busy turn and **tired** after half an hour; it is **confused** when a tool
just failed and **dizzy** when they keep failing. It **pleads** when it needs you, squints `^^` when it is
done, and falls **asleep** when the host goes quiet. It blinks, follows your pointer with its eyes, and
plays a short motion on each change — once, and then it rests. A board that keeps celebrating something
that finished an hour ago is noise.

dsh-agents-notch README · Sixteen faces：
**🫥 Never in the way**
Never takes focus, and steps aside when you pass over it: it fades and your click goes through. No shadow on your desktop. Hides under a full-screen app. 		**↗️ Open goes there**
Open, or a double-click, switches DeepSeek Harness to that session and brings it to the front — out of the taskbar or the tray.

dsh-agents-notch README · Sixteen faces：**📏 Honest numbers**
No context percentage without a real budget, no "2m ago" without a timestamp, and a grey tab when the host stops answering. **🎛️ A Settings pane of its own**
Settings → Agents Notch: size, anchor, display, rows, opacity, motion, how it reacts to the pointer, and which alerts pop up. A change lands on the next tick — nothing restarts.

dsh-agents-notch README · Sixteen faces：**🧘 Respects reduce-motion**
`motion: auto` follows Windows. With it off you get each state's settled face and nothing else. **📦 One command, no runtime**
~30 KB of JavaScript. The window fetches itself from the matching GitHub release, hash-verified — one self-contained file, no .NET to install.

dsh-agents-notch README · Requirements：- **Windows 10/11, x64.** The window is WPF and Win32 (topmost, no-activate, fullscreen detection):
  there is no macOS or Linux build. `package.json` declares `"os": ["win32"]`.
- **DeepSeek Harness.** Built and verified on **0.2.1-rc.2**. The host half reads `session/event`
  (`{ global: true }`), `ctx.webServer`, `ctx.agents` and `sessionQuery`, and the in-app half uses
  `uiWorkspace`; an older build may lack one. Nothing is checked before mounting — see
  [*Limits*](#limits-stated-plainly).
- **Node ≥ 22** for the plugin. **No .NET runtime**: the released window is self-contained.
- Optional: the **`session-finished`** plugin, which is what retires a finished row
  ([*What earns a row*](#what-earns-a-row)).

dsh-agents-notch README · Install：```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-agents-notch
```

Running the harness under another profile? Put its name in place of `web`.

The plugin is ~30 KB. The first time it runs, it downloads its window (one 65 MB file, no .NET runtime
needed) from this repo's GitHub release and checks it against the published SHA-256. A few seconds later
the notch is at the top of your screen.

dsh-agents-notch README · Install：**No notch?** Look at the last line of `$DSH_HOME\state\agents-notch\host-report.jsonl`: it says where
the host looked for the window, whether the download worked, and the command that fixes it.

dsh-agents-notch README · Configure：**The notch has a pane of its own: Settings → Agents Notch.** Size, anchor, display, rows, opacity,
motion and the text switches live there, and a change lands on the notch immediately — the window
re-reads its state on the next tick, so nothing restarts.

Three layers decide a value, each beating the one above it:

dsh-agents-notch README · Configure：
Every key, and how to set it in YAML
Defaults live in the package's own `cordis.patch.yml`. To change one, put a row **with the same id** in your profile's patch layer (`$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`) — a row without `insert:` is an override of a row that already exists: ```yaml - id: agents-notch config: contextBudget: 1000000 # your route's context window, in tokens anchor: top-right

dsh-agents-notch README · Configure：| key | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `spawnWindow` | `true` | `false` runs the host without a window — useful for tests |
| `pollMs` | `340` | how often the state file is rebuilt |
| `maxRows` | `6` | 3–10, how many sessions the board shows before its list scrolls |
| `contextBudget` | `null` | your route's context window in tokens; `null` = unknown (see below) |
| `contextHotAt` | `0.5` | the fraction where the bar turns amber — the route's compaction trigger |
| `anchor` | `top-center` | `top-center` · `top-left` · `top-right` |
| `screen` | `primary` | `primary` · `cursor` · `1` · `2` … (as Windows numbers them) |
| `scale` | `1` | 0.75–2 |
| `hideFullscreen` | `true` | hide under a full-screen app |
| `opacity` | `1` | 0.35–1, how much of the desktop the notch sits in front of |
| `motion` | `auto` | `auto` follows Windows' reduce-motion setting; `on` forces the animation, `off` draws each state's settled face and nothing else |
| `showProject` | `true` | the project name in the headline's sub line |
| `showDone` | `true` | `false` keeps finished sessions off the board entirely (and out of the count) |
| `hoverMode` | `ghost` | `ghost`
dsh-agents-notch README · Configure：</details>

dsh-agents-notch README · Honest numbers：`contextBudget` is **not** guessed. The context window belongs to the model route, and nothing in the session feed carries it, so this plugin defaults it to `null` — and with `null` you get a token count and no percentage, no bar and no amber. A percentage against an invented denominator is a lie that looks like information, which is worse than a number with units.

dsh-agents-notch README · Honest numbers：Set it to your route's real window (this build's DeepSeek V4 routes: `1000000`) and the percentage and
the bar appear.

dsh-agents-notch README · What earns a row：A session is on the board because **something happened to it**: it is working, it is blocked on an
approval or a question, it failed, or it finished and you have not closed it out. Merely being open
never earns a row, however many sessions are attached.

dsh-agents-notch README · What earns a row：Finished and failed rows do not expire on a timer. They leave when the harness's own close-out
verdict says so — the ✓ that the **`session-finished`** plugin puts in the sidebar, read over that
plugin's HTTP route, or the ✕ on the row. If that plugin is not installed, this one notices after three
failed probes and retires settled rows after 15 minutes instead, and says so in its report
(`host-report.jsonl`).

dsh-agents-notch README · What earns a row：When the host stops answering, the board stops pretending — the tab goes grey, the bot falls asleep, and the sub line dates the last heartbeat instead of repeating a summary nobody is updating:

dsh-agents-notch README · Limits, stated plainly：- **Windows only**, x64. No macOS or Linux build, and no partial one.
- **No DSH version is declared in the manifest**, so nothing gates a wrong install. It was built and
  tested on `0.2.1-rc.2`; if a field is missing on your build, the host keeps serving and the log
  says what failed rather than the tab lying.
- **Open needs the app's own window.** It switches sessions through the plugin's in-app half, so the app
  has to be running; the notch can bring its window back from the taskbar or the tray, but it cannot
  start the app.
- **`session-finished` is optional but recommended** — without it, closed-out sessions linger for
  the 15-minute fallback.
- **The window is not draggable**, by design: it is a fixed surface at the top of the screen, and a
  draggable one got dragged by accident. Move it with `anchor` and `screen`.
- **Two windows cannot coexist** — a named mutex makes the second instance exit.
- **The binary is unsigned**, so SmartScreen warns the first time you run it.
- **Quitting it from the tray is a one-hour dismissal, not forever**: the host brings the notch back,
  because a status board that can be lost by accide

dsh-agents-notch README · Uninstall：```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-agents-notch
Remove-Item -Recurse "$env:DSH_HOME\state\agents-notch"    # state, logs, window binary, unpack cache
```

dsh-agents-notch README · Develop：```powershell
npm test                      # 65 tests, node --test, no harness, no window, no network
npm run window:build          # dotnet build desktop/AgentsNotch.csproj -c Release
npm run window:publish        # self-contained single file + SHA256 into dist/win-x64

dsh-agents-notch README · 中文：**Agents Notch** 是一个 DeepSeek Harness 插件：在屏幕顶部挂一个始终置顶的“刘海”，每个会话一个小机器人，一眼就能看出
**哪个会话正在等你**。

dsh-agents-notch README · 中文：- **工作中**是缓慢转动的蓝色弧线，正在调用工具时标签底边会有光流过；**需要你**是琥珀色光圈；**完成**是绿色光圈和 `^^` 表情；**失败**是红色光圈和 `x x` 表情。
- 有会话需要你、失败或完成时，标签会短暂展开成提示，显示原因和 **Open** 按钮——一键切换到该会话，即使应用最小化或在托盘里。
- 从不挡路：鼠标经过时标签变成半透明，点击直接穿透到下面的窗口；停留 1.6 秒（或把鼠标推到屏幕顶边）才展开面板：最新变化的会话在顶部（标题、项目、上下文用量、正在运行的工具或等待的问题），其余会话列在下方，超出时可滚动。单击一行在大机器人上查看，双击或 **Open ↗** 切换到该会话。
- 机器人有十六种表情：思考、专注、疲惫、困惑、恳求、完成、睡着……
- 从不抢焦点，全屏应用下自动隐藏；没有真实的上下文预算就不显示百分比，宿主断开时标签变灰并注明最后心跳时间。
- 设置 → **Agents Notch** 有独立设置页：大小、位置、显示器、行数、不透明度、动效、悬停方式、提示类型，修改即时生效。

dsh-agents-notch README · 中文：```powershell dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-agents-notch ``` 仅支持 **Windows 10/11 x64**。插件本体约 30 KB，首次运行时会从对应版本的 GitHub Release 自动下载窗口程序并校验 SHA256，无需安装 .NET 运行时。
